problem: New, from the S3R-jobs-C1-1 fix. _leader_begun_near reads the group leader's birth time with '/bin/ps -o lstart=' and parses it with the fixed English format '%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y'. But ps inherits the caller's locale, and macOS ps formats lstart with strftime %c. Under en_GB.UTF-8 it prints 'Tue 24 Nov 18:27:07 2026', under de_DE.UTF-8 'Di. 24 Nov. 18:27:07 2026', and under fr_FR.UTF-8 'mar. 24 nov. 18:27:07 2026'. strptime then fails and the check answers False. The loss branch of attach then never kills the orphaned command group, so after a lost worker the restarted gate command runs beside the old one in the same worktree. That is the D6 kill that test_lost_worker_restarts_once asserts. Probe: test_lost_worker_restarts_once passes under LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 and fails under LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8 and LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8, with 'the orphaned command group survived the restart'. The suite passes on this machine only because it runs en_US. Linux procps may localise lstart too; that was not probed.
proposed_resolution: Run ps in the C locale: pass env={**os.environ, 'LC_ALL': 'C'} to the subprocess.run in _leader_begun_near (LC_ALL overrides LANG and LC_TIME). Or avoid date text altogether: read 'ps -o etime= -p <pgid>' ([[dd-]hh:]mm:ss, digits only) and compare now minus the elapsed time with the recorded time. Add a test that sets LC_ALL to en_GB.UTF-8 or de_DE.UTF-8 (monkeypatch.setenv, skipped when the locale is not installed) and asserts that _leader_begun_near(fresh_group, _now()) is True and that the lost-worker restart still kills the orphaned group.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/gates/env.py (start reads the record before the lock probe; _held_answer's running branch)
problem: Left by the S3R-jobs-C2-1 fix. It is the same snapshot class C2-1 named, in the branch the fix did not change, so the fix did not introduce it. start() reads the record before it probes the product lock, and _held_answer re-reads only when the snapshot says 'starting'. A snapshot that says 'running' is still acted on as read. Suppose a stale running record (its product dead, its lock free) is in the store and two start calls of one subject overlap. The second call can read the stale record before the first call takes the lock and unlinks it, and then find the lock held. At the same commit, the second call answers with the stale record and its dead pid. At another commit, it calls stop_products(subject), which by then finds the first call's fresh running record. It stops that product and starts a second one, so the first call's answer names a dead product (D14 says a second start at the same commit returns the first). Probe in a scratch copy, with a sleep between start()'s read and its lock probe. Stale record at the head commit: the first call answered pid 83191 (alive), and the second answered pid 999999 (the stale record's, dead). Stale record at another commit: both calls returned 0 with different pids, and the first call's product was dead. The C2-1 case itself (a 'starting' snapshot) answered both calls with the first product, still alive.
proposed_resolution: Decide on a record read after the lock probe in every branch. In start(), read the record after _acquire fails. In _held_answer, re-read the record before answering or replacing in the running branch as well. The first call may still be between taking the lock and unlinking the stale record, so also treat a running record whose pid is gone (os.kill(pid, 0) fails) while the lock is held as a start in progress: wait for a running record, as the starting branch does, and never answer from it or stop on it. Add tests with a stale running record at the head commit and at another commit: two overlapping starts, with the window widened, both return the same live pid.
